title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC0LD_1RD1RA_1RE0RB_0LA0RF_1LE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC0LD_1RD1RA_1RE0RB_0LA0RF_1LE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. This is the counter of 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1RD0RA_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD--- with its states renamed (A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A), started in a different state. Lean proves every ordinary sweep, every left-end sweep except the start of a nested run, and that the inner sweeps of a nested run follow the same digit rule; it runs 258,046 proved sweeps: no halt in the first 266,357,150,814 steps, where the third nested run starts. The cell simulator reaches 3·1011 steps, inside that nested run.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: One sweep, for every digit list
claims.text: Read a block 0 1^(3d+2) as the digit d. From the right end the head passes every odd digit, stops at the first even digit b (with the digit a on its left) and returns: a 0 (2k+1)… becomes (a+2) 0^(2k) 1… and a b (2k+1)… (b = 2i+2) becomes (a+1) 0^(b−1) 1 0^(2k) 1…, in 21 + 10b + Σ(20k+16) steps, for all values and any tape left of a.

claims.title: Sweeps at the left end
claims.text: A stop at the first digit grows the leftmost block 1^r by 6 (digit 0) or 3 (digit 2i+2); a carry through all digits at r = 3 adds two leading zeros and three cells on the left; at r = 6j+9 the leftmost block becomes 1^3 and 2j+3 zeros. The other phase of the right end (0 1^4 C>0) turns the last digit 1 into 2 0.

claims.title: From blank tape to sweep 29
claims.text: After 5,512 steps (after two nested runs, checked step by step) the tape is 1^3, the digits 0 0 1 1 1 0 2 and ten digits 1, and the right end in its other phase 0 1^4 C>0.

claims.title: No halt in the first 266,357,150,814 steps
claims.text: From the proved configuration at step 5,512, 258,046 sweeps on run-length coded digits (runR), each covered by a proved rule: no halt in the first 266,357,150,814 steps. The next sweep is the start of the third nested run, at 1^12 | 1 1 5 1^9 3 1^129022 | 0 1 C>0 (run_stops). (The earlier digit-list run no_halt_1595848115 is kept.)

claims.title: Inside a nested run: the same counter
claims.text: A carry through odd digits, the first one 1, into 1^(6j+6) turns the block into 1^3 and 2j+1 digits 0 and turns the head back before the right end (nest_sweep). From there the inner sweeps change the digits by exactly the outer rule (core_zero, core_even, with any tape right of the pass), their right end alternates between two phases, and every second sweep eats one passed digit 1 (inner_X_zero, inner_X_even, inner_Y_zero, inner_Y_even).

claims.title: Sweeps on run-length coded digits
claims.text: nextR does one sweep on digits coded as runs ((d, c): c copies of d, from the right end), covering the same cases as next; whenever it answers, the machine makes that sweep in that many steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3·10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The cell-by-cell simulator c/brec.c finds no halt in the first 3·1011 steps. That bound ends inside the third nested run (which starts at step 266,357,150,814 on a tape of about 7.7·105 cells). c/dsim.c, which runs the proved sweep rules on run-length coded digits, reproduces the Lean run and stops at the same sweep.

claims.title: The rest of a nested run
claims.text: Passed digits 3, 5, … are eaten in another phase pattern; the inner counter has its own left-end events, including nested runs inside the nested run; the run ends with the right end in its other phase when the passed region is used up. Seen in simulation (on both machines), not formalized. In this run nested runs come at sweeps 5, 28 and 258,075.

claims.title: Where a halt would come from
claims.text: Following the table backwards, the machine halts exactly when C reads a 0 followed by 0 1 1 (a right-moving head meeting 0 0 1 1). No proved sweep produces it; a halt would have to come from a nested run.
claims.where: README, section Where it could halt

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Closing it needs the whole nested run as a theorem (shared with the other machine), so that the sweep program is total, and an argument that nested runs always end in a sweep configuration. The third nested run, about 3·10<sup>11</sup> steps long, is beyond a cell-by-cell native_decide check.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but we know what it is doing: it counts, exactly like its twin 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1RD0RA_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD--- with the states renamed. The tape is a row of blocks of ones, each block a digit, and once per trip of the head the number goes up by one. Now and then a carry falls off the left end and the machine starts counting inside its own count. Lean proves every ordinary trip and the inner trips of a nested count, and runs the counter up to its third nested count: no halt in 2.66·10<sup>11</sup> steps.

facts.text: No halt, proved in Lean: 258,046 proved trips, up to the third nested run.
The trip rule, for all digit values; inside a nested run too.
No halt, cell by cell in C (inside the third nested run).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.497).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,531 cells (12 left of the start, 34,840 right), with a density of 1s of 0.557.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: Cut the tape at its 0s. Every piece is a block of ones, and almost every block has 2, 5, 8, 11, … ones: 3d+2 ones for a whole number d. Call that block the digit d. Only the leftmost block (three ones for most of the run) is not a digit.

sections.heading: One trip of the head
html: From the right end the head walks left in state E, rewriting each block it crosses as alternating 0 1. A block of odd length is crossed; at the first block of even length (an even digit) it turns at once, walks back to the right end in state B and rebuilds every block it crossed, now three cells further right. So every trip adds exactly three cells.

Above: the digits 1 0 3 1. The left pass crosses 1 and 3 (odd), stops at the 0; the 0 merges into the 1 on its left, which becomes 3; the crossed 3 comes back as 0 0 1 and the 1 as 1. Exactly (for all values, proved in Lean): with a the digit left of the stop digit b and odd digits 2k+1 after it,

stop digitbeforeafter
b = 0a 0 (2k₁+1) … (2kₙ+1)(a+2) 0^(2k₁) 1 … 0^(2kₙ) 1
b = 2i+2a b (2k₁+1) …(a+1) 0^(b−1) 1 0^(2k₁) 1 …
The trip takes 21 + 10b + Σ(20k + 16) steps: it is linear in the length of the tape it crosses, so the n-th trip takes about 8n steps and the run is quadratic: the square-root growth of the tape.

sections.heading: An odometer
html: Read it like a car's odometer. The rightmost even digit is the one that moves. Odd digits to its right are like the 9s in 1999 + 1: the increment turns each of them into zeros and a 1 and carries on to the left. A long run of 1s is a run of carries already made, crossed for free. Here the active digits sit in one cluster at the left end of the tape, and the run of 1s to their right grows by one every two trips (24,985 of them at trip 50,000).

This is digit for digit, step for step, the counter of 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1RD0RA_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD---: the two machines write the same blocks and take the same number of steps for every trip; they differ in their state names and in how the head turns at the stop digit (this one turns as soon as it reaches the even block: L 0 11 E>0 becomes L 1111 B> in 9 steps).

sections.heading: At the left end: counting inside the count
html: When no even digit is left, the head reaches the leftmost block 1^r. If the first digit is even it merges into that block (r grows by 6 or 3). If every digit is odd the carry falls off the end: for r = 3 the tape grows three cells to the left and gets two new leading zeros, for r = 9, 15, 21, … the block shrinks back to three ones and leaves zeros behind. All of this is proved.
If r is even (6, 12, 18, …) something new happens: a nested run. Next section.

sections.heading: The nested run
html: On its way left the head has rewritten every digit it passed (a digit 1 becomes the word 0 0 1 0 1 0). At an even leftmost block 1^(6j+6) it does not go back to the right end. The block becomes 1^3 followed by 2j+1 digits 0, and the head turns at a frontier just left of the passed region. Left of the frontier is a new, small counter; right of it the passed region plays the part that blank tape plays for the outer counter.

Lean proves that every inner trip changes the inner digits by exactly the same rule as an ordinary trip, that the inner right end alternates between two shapes, and that every second inner trip eats one passed digit 1. Not yet proved: passed digits 3, 5, …, the inner counter’s own left-end events (which can start a nested run inside the nested run), and the end of the run.

From blank tape this happens at trips 5 and 28, while the tape is short (these are checked step by step), and again at trip 258,075, step 266,357,150,814, from 1^12 | 1 1 5 1^9 3 1^129022. That third nested run, on a tape of about 770,000 cells, should last about 3·1011 steps; it is where the proved run stops.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only missing transition is F reading a 1. Following the table backwards, the machine halts exactly when C reads a 0 followed by 0 1 1: a head moving right meets 0 0 1 1. No proved trip ever shows it that pattern, so a halt would have to come out of a nested run. The open question is whether a nested run, which can contain nested runs of its own, always ends cleanly.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel. The pieces of a trip (lean/Rules.lean); a whole trip for every digit list (sweep_zero, sweep_even); the left-end cases except the nested run (raw_zero, raw_even, carry3_sweep, carry9_sweep, phase2_sweep); the configuration at step 5,512 (reach_D0); the trips on run-length coded digits (nextR_sound, lean/Rle.lean); the start of a nested run and its inner trips (nest_sweep, inner_X_zero, …, lean/Inner.lean).
Lean, native_decide. 258,046 proved trips: no halt in the first 266,357,150,814 steps (no_halt_long, lean/RunLong.lean), and the next trip is the third nested run (run_stops).
Trusted (C). c/brec.c, cell by cell: no halt in 3·1011 steps.
Open. The nested run as a whole, and whether nested runs always end cleanly.

family: counter in blocks 1^(3d+2), with nested runs of itself at the left end
summary: The same counter as 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1RD0RA_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD--- under renamed states: digits are blocks of 3d+2 ones, one sweep per increment, and a carry into an even leftmost block starts a nested run of the counter inside the tape. Lean gives no halt in 2.66·10^11 steps, up to the start of the third nested run.
